summary: Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1997, earning a DLitt) under Minoru Hara. He worked at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (1975) and Kokugakuin University (1986–1995 as lecturer, associate professor, and professor).
Keiji Iwata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1948). He held academic posts at Otani University (~1958–1968) and the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1974–1980).
Keiji Kokubu was a philosophy scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, Nanzan University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Keiji Nishitani was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitarō Nishida and Hajime Tanabe, and at the University of Freiburg under Martin Heidegger. He held posts at Otani University and Kyoto University (professor 1943–1964).

Keiki Yabuki was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku Fukushi, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He taught at Tendai Sect University, Shukyo University, Nihon University, Tokyo Higher Normal School, the University of Tokyo (~1924–1934), and Taisho University (~1926–1939).

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Academic affiliations include posts as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies (attested 2015).

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Durham University (~2007–2011) under Robin Coningham. He studied at and held a post at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016), later joining La Trobe University (2016).
Keishi Renja is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied in the doctoral program at Taisho University (attested 2013) and served as a research student there.

Keishin Okamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1949–1959). He held faculty posts at Koyasan University (1959–1973; guest professor 2005–2009) and Kochi University (~1963–1995; professor ~1974–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his doctorate at Tohoku University (-1964). He held professorships at Tohoku University (~1970–1993) and Rissho University (~1970–1993), served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1993–2001), and visited Mahidol University.

Keisuke Fujii is an architectural historian and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1986). He taught at the University of Tokyo (1982–2018) and served as a guest professor at Tokyo University of the Arts (~2018).

Keith Dowman is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, and Kangyur Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1977–1982). He served as lecturer and professor at Shuchiin University (~1987–2008) and held posts at Taisho University, including institute director (~2012–2019).

Keizaburo Mizuno was an art historian in Japanese and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956). He worked at Tokyo National Museum, became professor emeritus at Tokyo University of the Arts, and directed the Niigata Prefectural and Hanzomon museums.
Keizo Kojima was a philosophy scholar who studied at Hitotsubashi University and under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He later held an academic post at Sophia University.

Kelsang Gyatso was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Ngamring Chöde, Jampa Ling, Tashi Lhunpo, and Sera Monastery (~1945–1959) under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre (1977) and founded the New Kadampa Tradition (1991).

Kelsey Alise Seymour is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018). She was a visiting predoctoral fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).
Kemo Jin was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He held an academic post at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

Ken McLeod is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner and scholar who earned an MSc at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1970) and studied under Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa. He taught at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985) and founded Unfettered Mind (1990).
Kendall Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.
